berserker: clock 2:45 to OT 1:38 (Hero form, 'Savage Survival'): five deployments, all left lane — [3, 10] and [4, 10] as defensive bodies on his own half, and [3, 15], [2, 15], [2, 14] at the river as the Graveyard's tank. She is never sent alone at a tower; every river placement is within 1-2 s of a Graveyard cast.

clock 2:33: the ability is what makes the Graveyard playable for him — 'Normally I wouldn't, but because I have the ability... I can pop the ability now, keep it alive, but it's going to tank for the graveyard for a decent amount of time to get us some extra damage, maybe a shot.'

clock 1:11: pops it on defence and gets the game's biggest damage swing (enemy left tower 2809 -> 1560 across clock 1:09-1:05): 'Let's pop the ability here... look the berserker. Oh my god, it killed the spirit. Look at all that damage. Okay, maybe there isn't a reduction.' Earlier, at clock 2:03, he had read it the other way: 'It looks like it does reduce tower damage whenever it's in the ability... it would do more if there wasn't a reduction' (the hero card confirms -75% Crown Tower damage for 4 s).

Berserker graveyard here and then if we pop the ability, it should just live long enough to take the tower... GG's. Nice win.' He also declines the ability once, at clock 0:41 ('Nah, we can't ability'), and rates the 3-elixir cost as forgiving: 'you do have room to do bad abilities' (clock 0:13).

clock 1:19: the standard package is Graveyard plus a Berserker at the river to tank, not a spell to protect it: 'let's go for the graveyard berserker here. Just be annoying as annoying as we possibly can, especially cuz he had no berserker in cycle, so it's going to force out a lot more elixir.'

He never builds a dedicated answer, letting the Knight/Barbarian Barrel/Furnace shell that is already there handle it; his left tower still takes steady unattributed chip through both drills.
skeletons: clock 2:42, 0:50, 0:32 and 0:04 (opponent): the recurring cycle card in both lanes; Barbarian Barrel plus Knight is Ryley's standing answer — 'Let's barbarian barrel here, take this out. Good defense' (clock 0:25).
bomber: clock 2:26 through OT (opponent): his main support, repeatedly walking Ryley's left lane ([7, 24], [4, 21], [7, 20], [6, 24], [4, 16], [3, 13]). The Furnace + Ice Spirit + Knight defence exists mostly to stop it: 'Good defense should take this all out' (clock 0:51).
giant-snowball: clock 0:58 and 0:53 (opponent, Evolution): named twice by Ryley and never cleanly detected — 'He might get a snowball down' and 'Yeah, there's the Evo snow.' He spaces his Ice Spirit and Furnace rather than stacking them into it.
rocket: clock 0:28: mentioned, not seen — 'Let's go for the Knight here. He might go for a rocket.' No Rocket damage is recorded on his side in this game.
magic-archer: clock 1:39: mentioned only, as the one hero he rates near the Berserker — 'I don't know if there's any hero that will be as good as this one except maybe the magic archer, but the archer might get nerfed in the final balance changes. I really hope it does.'
goblins: clock 0:05: mentioned only, as the reference point for a cheap hero ability — 'unlike some heroes, right, like the ability being so cheap like goblins, you can never really do a bad one.'

bullets: Game 3 of a four-deck Hero Berserker showcase; Ryley names the list himself at clock 2:47 — 'now we're going to be playing with graveyard poison' — and wins it in overtime.

One-lane plan: every offensive commitment is Graveyard on the enemy left tower ([1, 24]-[1, 26]) with the Hero Berserker landing at the river to tank and Poison behind it (clock 2:33, 1:19, 0:46, 0:15, OT 1:38). The Berserker replaces the usual Barbarian Barrel bridge tank because 'Savage Survival' keeps her alive through the tower: 'Normally I wouldn't [graveyard], but because I have the ability... it's going to tank for the graveyard for a decent amount of time.'

Defence is entirely on his own half and entirely in the lane the opponent attacks: Knight in front of the tower, Barbarian Barrel and Ice Spirit on top, Furnace and Goblin Hut in the centre ([8, 8]-[9, 11]) to drip spirits and Spear Goblins into both jobs at once.

Spawner chip decides the game as much as the Graveyard does — 'Furnace is on the tower. Let's go. Good damage' (clock 0:03) — and he stacks huts on purpose: 'let's Goblin Hut first because I think he can't really take this out, and stocking up the Goblin Huts could be pretty nice for us' (clock 0:32).

Result: enemy left tower ground 3052 -> 210 while his own left holds at 1067; the finish is Berserker, then Graveyard, then the ability in overtime (OT 1:31): 'if we pop the ability, it should just live long enough to take the tower... GG's. Nice win.'

new_deck.rationale: Two spawners plus Knight/Barbarian Barrel/Ice Spirit defend and chip while a single repeatable Graveyard + Poison package is the only offence, which is the control pattern rather than cycle or bait.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck plays one lane and one push: Graveyard on the enemy tower with the Hero Berserker dropped at the river to tank it, and Poison ahead of the Skeletons to clear the cheap answers. The Hero's "Savage Survival" (3 elixir, 4 seconds, cannot drop below 1 HP) turns a 2-elixir troop into a tank that survives the Crown Tower long enough for the Skeletons to accumulate, which is why Ryley casts Graveyards he says he otherwise would not. Behind it, Furnace and Goblin Hut sit in the centre of his own half, so the same buildings feed defensive bodies against Goblin Drill and Bomber pressure and passive chip into the tower he is attacking. Knight, Barbarian Barrel and Ice Spirit cover the ground defence cheaply enough that the 9-elixir Graveyard + Poison + ability package can be repeated every rotation. The cost is that the ability's -75% Crown Tower damage means the Berserker chips very little herself, and the deck has no air answer beyond the Furnace spirits.
